importance_ranking.reason: Dome shelters have extreme visual sub-type variation — a geodesic PVC fabric glamping dome, a polycarbonate institutional dome, and an industrial metal-sheet dome shed are visually unrecognisable as the same product category. Buyers use the image to identify product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Span/diameter and cover material are non-interchangeable primary shortlisting criteria — a buyer needing a 10m glamping dome cannot evaluate a 30m industrial storage dome. Listings without these specs cannot be shortlisted regardless of price or supplier quality.

Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive but dome shelter prices vary enormously with span, frame material, and cover type — price is only comparable after spec equivalence is confirmed. Large custom installations are always negotiated; listed price is a budget entry point, not a final figure.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard modular domes (up to ~10m diameter) are quoted per piece; larger custom spans are quoted per sq ft of covered area; turnkey installation projects are quoted per project. Unit must be shown to prevent price misreading across these three quoting conventions.
importance_ranking.reason: Three distinct quoting conventions coexist in this market — per piece, per sq ft, and per project. A buyer comparing prices across listings without visible units cannot make a valid comparison; the confusion is a real and documented market ambiguity.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in the Indian dome shelter market — the market is fragmented across regional fabricators in Jaipur, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, and Nagpur; buyers search by spec and application, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Dome shelters are structural products with significant installation dependency — buyers evaluate fabrication capability, installation track record, and post-sale service availability during vendor selection, particularly for large-span or permanent structures.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Span width is the primary product class separator — a buyer needing 20m coverage cannot substitute a 10m dome, and price scales non-linearly with span, making it the single largest price driver in the category.

Cover material defines the product's structural character and application suitability — PVC fabric geodesic, polycarbonate, and metal sheet domes are non-interchangeable across glamping, institutional, and industrial applications, with significant price deltas between material types.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Institutional, industrial, and event buyers specify required wind load compliance (typically per IS 875 Part 3) as a procurement criterion; sellers need this to confirm structural adequacy and provide certified designs.

Industrial storage buyers require minimum interior clearance for forklift or vehicle access, and event buyers need headroom specifications; sellers cannot confirm suitability without knowing the required height.

Event organisers and institutional buyers (schools, public venues) require fire-retardant certified cover material for safety compliance and event permits; this is a binary eligibility criterion that eliminates non-compliant suppliers.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Diameter defines the scale of the structure and is non-interchangeable — sellers need this to confirm manufacturing capability, material quantities, and to price accurately.

Covering material defines the product type and application suitability — sellers who manufacture PVC fabric geodesic domes cannot supply polycarbonate or metal sheet domes, making this a primary routing spec.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers who fabricate only permanent fixed structures cannot supply portable or relocatable domes — this spec routes the RFQ to the correct supplier type and determines anchoring, foundation, and pricing approach.
